title: ConQEC: Concolic Testing for Quantum Error-Correcting Code Implementations
authors: Zihao Li, Ji Guan, Mingsheng Ying
abstract: Quantum error-correcting code (QECC) implementations are hybrid software-control systems: measured syndromes drive decoder dispatch, recovery actions, and logical checks. Existing QECC verification techniques can prove formal obligations, and general quantum testing can expose final failures, but developers still lack a scalable testing workflow that generates concrete faults and explains where a QECC repair path first diverges. This paper presents ConQEC, to our knowledge the first concolic testing framework for QECC implementations. By combining concrete (Pauli) fault replay with symbolic repair-path constraints, ConQEC generates tests that expose not only final logical failures but also fault--syndrome--decoder--recovery (FSDR) diagnostics: the injected fault, observed syndrome, decoder decision, recovery action, oracle result, and earliest divergent stage. Its symbolic encoding of Pauli faults, syndrome predicates, decoder and recovery relations, and oracle checks enables this diagnostic workflow to scale beyond exponentially increasing amplitude-level quantum-state reasoning. We implemented ConQEC and evaluated it on generated source-level QECC families and public QECC artifacts with up to thousands of qubits. ConQEC detects the seeded bug in every experimental case and reports a replay-valid, fault-localizing FSDR witness for each.
summary: This paper introduces ConQEC, a novel concolic testing framework designed to rigorously test Quantum Error-Correcting Code (QECC) implementations. It moves beyond simple failure detection by generating concrete faults and providing a detailed, localized diagnostic witness (FSDR) pinpointing the exact stage of failure in the error-correction pipeline. This approach scales to thousands of qubits by using symbolic constraints over the discrete repair path rather than full quantum state simulation.
main_problem: Developing a scalable testing workflow for Quantum Error-Correcting Code (QECC) implementations that can pinpoint the exact stage where a repair path fails, rather than just detecting a final logical error.
main_result: The ConQEC framework successfully detects seeded bugs in large-scale QECC artifacts (thousands of qubits) and provides a detailed, replay-valid Fault–Syndrome–Decoder–Recovery (FSDR) witness for localization.
method: It employs concolic testing by combining concrete Pauli fault replay with symbolic constraint solving over the QECC repair path stages (fault, syndrome, decoder, recovery).
model_or_system: The system under test is a QECC implementation, modeled as a hybrid software-control pipeline that processes injected Pauli faults to restore logical quantum information.
key_observables: Fault-Syndrome-Decoder-Recovery (FSDR) diagnostics, Pair-Mask Coverage, and the earliest divergent stage ($\delta$) in the repair path.
important_parameters: The framework scales to thousands of qubits, overcoming the exponential state space limitations of amplitude-level quantum testing.
main_assumptions: The method assumes the ability to define compact, symbolic constraints over the discrete stages of the QECC repair path, and requires access to a reference contract for comparison.

paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem of QECC testing, details the ConQEC concolic framework by defining the symbolic constraints over the FSDR path, demonstrates its application to generate fault-localizing witnesses, and validates its scalability on large-scale and public artifacts.
why_interesting: While focused on software verification, the scalability demonstrated for large-scale quantum systems and the rigorous diagnostic output (pinpointing the exact failure stage) are highly relevant for debugging complex quantum hardware control stacks.
